title: One Hot Encoding and Feature Engineering
body:
A Canadian study of workers in the 1980s collected the following information:
• wage (hourly in dollars)
• edu (years)
• $$	ext{job\_type}$$ (1 for blue collar, $$2$$ for white collar, and $$3$$ for managerial)

A data scientist fitted a model with wage as the response, and the other two variables as features , where $$	ext{job\_type}$$ was one-hot encoded). The resulting fitted model was $$\hat{y}=x\cdot\hat{ eta}, $$ where $$\hat{ eta}=(-8,3,6,-3)**{T},$$ i.e.
$$\hat{y}=-8+3x_{edu}+6x_{m}-3x_{b}$$
where $$y$$ is the hourly wage, $$x_{edu}$$ is years of education, and the other two variables are the dummies for managerial and blue collar workers, respectively.
